newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's ASB Bank lifts Q3 profit by 24 percent.
newsitem.headline: NZ's ASB Bank lifts Q3 profit by 24 percent.

text.p: New Zealand's ASB Bank said on Tuesday the impetus gained from strong asset growth over the past year had helped it lift unaudited after-tax operating profit by 24 percent to NZ$18.2 million for the three months ended September 30.

However, it said that momentum was gradually decreasing. While the bank was forecasting a sound profit for the first six months of the current financial year, it did not anticipate maintaining the present rate of growth.
Total operating revenue during the three month period increased by 13 percent to $93.7 million and operating profit before tax by 22 percent to NZ$28.1 million.
Provision for taxation was up 14 percent to $9.9 million.

"The home mortgage market was extremely buoyant throughout our 1996 financial year and assisted us in increasing our total assets to $9.1 billion at June 30, 1996, an increase of 22 percent. The flow on benefits have given us a strong start to the current financial year.
"A quieter housing market in the last three months saw asset growth slow, increasing by 16 percent, on an annualised basis, to $9.45 billion," the bank said in a statement.
It said recent indications were that increased confidence was starting to return to the housing market.
